evidence: All ten uplift code repositories have active protect-main rulesets, required validate checks, non-fast-forward and deletion protections, resolved review-thread requirements, read-only default workflow permissions, secret scanning, and push protection.
Current-head CI and CodeQL runs succeeded and the GitHub alert APIs reported zero open code-scanning, Dependabot, or secret-scanning alerts.
Full-history redacted gitleaks scans found zero secrets in the ten uplift code repositories; three backend matches were reviewed as synthetic test metadata or a repository identifier.
Shared packages are immutable public GitHub Packages published from exact tarballs with GitHub attestations and recorded SHA-256 digests.
All eight deployed service images use exact runtime digests, have commit tags and cosign signature manifests, and are restricted to trusted source repositories by the backend runtime manifest.
Local locked dependency installs, unit/integration CI, npm high-severity audit, CycloneDX generation, CodeQL, image vulnerability scans, and image secret scans were reviewed.
No service repository stores deployment secrets. Backend runtime manifests mount only stage-specific RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, backend API, Qwen, or reconciliation files.
RabbitMQ producer/consumer identities, PostgreSQL stage roles, and backend persistence/publication API tokens are distinct and least-privilege in the source-controlled identity maps and validators.

LOCAL_AI_API_KEY is explicitly retained as the source for only the approval and translation Qwen credential files by issue #66 and backend credential-readiness run 30445298275; no credential material was read.
Grafana management credentials remain infra-owned; the backend receives only Prometheus and Loki write credentials.

External probes found only SSH, HTTP, and HTTPS open. PostgreSQL, AMQP, RabbitMQ management/metrics, worker admin, node-exporter, PostgreSQL exporter, and RabbitMQ exporter ports were closed or filtered.
backend.nutsnews.com served a valid public TLS certificate and health endpoint.
Fetcher policy rejects non-HTTP protocols, localhost, private, link-local, metadata, credential-bearing, and disallowed redirect destinations; focused tests passed.
The uplift vhost, route queues, exchanges, and users are isolated from the legacy worker.
Service identities cannot configure RabbitMQ, administer the broker, read unrelated queues, or publish outside their declared exchanges.
RabbitMQ canary run 30217775773 and clean-rebuild recovery run 30215207093 passed; broker contents are recoverable from the PostgreSQL stage ledger.
Each stage has a distinct PostgreSQL role and schema boundary; permission proof run 30024831874 checks table, sequence, function, schema, database, cross-stage, and public-schema privileges.
The proof's transient write checks roll back and the security review itself executed no database writes.
Backups are encrypted and off-host; secrets and RabbitMQ live message storage are intentionally restored from their owning systems rather than copied into backup artifacts.
Worker database endpoints reject missing and invalid bearer credentials with HTTP 401.
Persistence and publication tokens are command-scoped and reconciliation endpoints accept fixed bounded actions only.
Production commands fail closed unless backend PostgreSQL is primary, cutover state is approved, production writes are explicitly enabled, and the existing Worker DB API write guard also passes.
Only approval and translation receive Qwen credentials; model calls are bounded by input size, concurrency, and timeout.
OpenAI fallback is disabled and its shadow budget is zero.
Structured logs and metrics exclude prompt bodies, article bodies, authentication material, and provider response bodies.
Grafana Cloud management stays in nutsnews-infra while backend services have remote-write-only credentials.
Runtime status, queue consumer, cancellation, dropped-channel, DLQ, queue-depth, and stage telemetry are checked by protected backend workflows.
Metrics run 30405452541, logs run 30405452566, and complete soak report run 30405550709 passed with immutable artifacts.
Protected backend workflows own deployments, restarts, recovery, credential audit, and read-only runtime checks.
Current production-backend protections fail closed while an approval is required; this review did not bypass an environment wait.
Legacy ingestion, Cloudflare routing, DNS failover, cutover state, and production writes are independent of every reviewed shadow operation.

findings.title: Workflow dispatch and repository data were interpolated directly into privileged shell scripts
findings.disposition: Affected backend workflows now pass dispatch and repository data through step environment variables. A repository-wide validator rejects direct shell interpolation and non-immutable action references.
verification: zizmor reports no high-severity backend workflow findings

findings.title: Uplift repositories use trusted action release tags rather than immutable action commit SHAs

risk_acceptance.rationale: Required validation, read-only default permissions, exact current workflow resolutions, branch protections, and no production writes constrain exposure.
risk_acceptance.required_follow_up: Pin all external actions to reviewed commit SHAs before production-readiness approval.

findings.title: Some publish workflows restore dependency caches in artifact-producing jobs

risk_acceptance.rationale: Publishing is main-only, package lockfiles are enforced, image identity is exact-digest and signed, and production writes remain disabled.
risk_acceptance.required_follow_up: Remove publish-job caches or isolate them from untrusted pull-request cache namespaces before production-readiness approval.

findings.title: Runtime images retain the npm CLI and development-only dependency content

risk_acceptance.rationale: The seven high/critical scanner matches per image are confined to an unused npm CLI or a development-only package and are not reachable by the node dist/src/index.js runtime command. Images run non-root and image secret scans are clean.
risk_acceptance.required_follow_up: Use production-only multi-stage images without npm CLI or development dependencies and rescan before production-readiness approval.

findings.title: Four service publish workflows do not attach an image SBOM attestation

risk_acceptance.rationale: All services generate CycloneDX dependency SBOMs in CI and every deployed image is SHA-tagged, exact-digest pinned, scanned, and signed.
risk_acceptance.required_follow_up: Attach image SBOM attestations for approval, translation, persistence, and publication before production-readiness approval.

findings.title: Fetcher DNS policy has a resolution-to-connect time-of-check/time-of-use window

risk_acceptance.rationale: Feed URLs come from the controlled scheduler path, redirects are revalidated, private and metadata addresses are blocked, host-local privileged endpoints require separate credentials, and production writes are disabled.
risk_acceptance.required_follow_up: Bind outbound connections to the policy-validated address or use an equivalently rebinding-safe agent before production-readiness approval.

findings.title: Approval and translation derive service Qwen files from one retained source credential

risk_acceptance.rationale: The credential controls only the Qwen provider and cannot administer RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, the backend API, Grafana, deployment, DNS, or failover.
risk_acceptance.required_follow_up: Split provider credentials if supported before production-readiness approval, otherwise explicitly renew this provider-scoped acceptance.

findings.title: Scheduled read-only monitoring uses repository-level host and API credentials

risk_acceptance.rationale: The scheduled workflows run fixed source-controlled read-only commands from protected main with read-only workflow permissions; state-changing backend operations remain environment-protected.
risk_acceptance.required_follow_up: Evidence a forced-command or equivalently restricted read-only host identity before production-readiness approval.

findings.title: Uplift repository rulesets require pull requests but zero approving reviews

risk_acceptance.rationale: Rulesets require current validation and resolved review threads and block destructive history changes; all services remain shadow-only.
risk_acceptance.required_follow_up: Reassess reviewer requirements when an independent maintainer is available and before production-readiness approval.

scanner_dispositions.summary: The scanner findings are confined to the unused npm CLI dependency tree or a development-only package; no finding is reachable from the production service entry point. SEC-124-004 retains the image-content hardening risk.
Two synthetic redaction-test strings and one repository identifier matched generic API-key heuristics. GitHub secret scanning reports zero open alerts.
Eight high-severity shell template-injection findings and additional direct shell expressions were removed. Remaining findings are low-severity pinned ad-hoc tooling installations.

acceptance_criteria.evidence: The only high source finding is remediated; scanner high/critical matches were reachability-triaged as not affected and the unnecessary image content remains tracked as medium SEC-124-004.
Package tarball digests and attestations, image source commits, publish runs, exact runtime digests, signatures, locked audits, SBOM generation, and image scan dispositions are recorded.
Source maps and permission proofs isolate RabbitMQ routes, PostgreSQL schemas, backend API commands, Qwen access, and Grafana write-only telemetry.
Production provider, cutover state, production-writes flag, and backend API write guard must all pass; current state is shadow with production writes disabled.
No reviewed operation changes legacy ingestion, DNS, Cloudflare routing, failover, cutover, or production-write state.

rollback.review_artifacts: Revert the review pull request; no runtime state was created by the review.
rollback.workflow_hardening: Revert only the source commit if necessary. Environment indirection preserves workflow inputs and operation semantics and performs no host or deployment change.
